result.summary: The environment is a typical residential street featuring row houses with a continuous, well-maintained concrete sidewalk. Pedestrian safety is supported by the presence of a clear walkway, but compromised by the lack of a buffer from the roadway and visual obstructions caused by on-street parking.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicle
hazards.description: The white car parked at the curb blocks the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians, particularly shorter individuals or children, who might step into the street.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the nearest intersection to improve visibility and shorten crossing distances for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Add a planting strip or street trees between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a physical and psychological buffer from moving traffic.

result.summary: This is a residential street with sidewalks on both sides, though they are narrow and lack a buffer from the roadway. There are no marked pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures visible in the immediate vicinity, and parked vehicles may obstruct sightlines.

hazards.description: There are no designated or marked crossing points for pedestrians visible along this stretch of road.
